title: PGIMER Puts Eye Emergency Teams on Special Diwali Roster, November 8-10
excerpt: Chandigarh's PGIMER will run dedicated eye-emergency arrangements at its Advanced Eye Centre through the Diwali weekend, with a published emergency mobile number.
body:
• PGIMER Chandigarh's Department of Ophthalmology has put special eye-emergency arrangements in place from November 8 to 10, 2026, covering the Diwali festivities.
  • A dedicated emergency roster will staff the Advanced Eye Centre, with residents instructed to be physically present and manage cases in consultation with the consultant on call.
  • For eye emergencies during this period, PGIMER lists mobile 9814014464 and Advanced Eye Centre Emergency extension 6117.
  • All Diwali-related emergency cases will be systematically documented — patient details, nature of injury and treatment — for monitoring and continuity of care.

The Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh has put special arrangements in place for eye emergencies during Diwali, its Department of Ophthalmology announced on November 5. The arrangements run from November 8 to 10, 2026, "in view of the possibility of eye injuries and other emergencies during the Diwali festivities," the institute said in a statement reported by India News Calling.

How the roster will work

A dedicated emergency roster has been prepared to manage all eye emergencies during the period. Residents have been instructed to adhere strictly to the duty roster, ensure their physical presence at the Advanced Eye Centre, and manage all cases in consultation with the consultant on call, the statement said. Teams attending to non-Diwali-related peripheral emergency calls will also continue managing those patients until discharge or transfer to the appropriate clinic.

Prof. Usha Singh, Professor and Head of the Department of Ophthalmology at PGIMER, is leading the department making the arrangements. The institute placed special emphasis on systematic documentation of every Diwali-related emergency case, including patient details, the nature of the injury and the treatment provided, to ensure proper monitoring and continuity of care.

Why the dates are November 8 to 10

The roster is timed to the festival itself rather than the announcement. Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 this year, and the days immediately after a festival night are when eye-injury cases that were first treated locally, or that worsened overnight, are referred onward. By running the dedicated arrangements through Tuesday, November 10, PGIMER covers the festival day and the two days after it, instead of standing the teams down once the main night ends. The announcement was made on November 5, giving families in the region three days to note the Advanced Eye Centre contacts before the first firecrackers are lit.

Who this is for, and the numbers to keep

PGIMER is the referral hospital for Chandigarh and large parts of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, which is why its Diwali roster matters beyond the city: firecracker eye injuries are typically referred there from across the region. If an eye is injured during the festival, the contacts PGIMER lists for this period are mobile 9814014464 and the Advanced Eye Centre Emergency extension 6117. Save both before November 8 — they are the fastest route to the team that will actually be on duty.
